answer: Your records do not show a blood clot in your lung. In July 2025 (on 8 July) you had a CT angiography of your chest, a scan done specifically to look for a clot in the lungs (a pulmonary embolism). The report says there was no pulmonary embolism, your lungs were clear, and there was no fluid around the lungs or heart. The record lists a possible pulmonary embolism from that time as ruled out. The same day a blood test called D-dimer came back high (0.92 mg/L FEU; the reference is 0.49 or lower). D-dimer is a sensitive test, so a high result can happen for many reasons, and the scan is what settled the question. Your records from that time also list chest wall pain, which was marked resolved by 22 July 2025. Your medication list has no blood thinner. If you remember symptoms or a different scan, please bring that up with your doctor, since the records I can see may not include everything.
short: July 2025 CT angiography of the chest showed no pulmonary embolism; lungs clear. Pulmonary embolism is recorded as ruled out. A same-day D-dimer was mildly high, which the scan explained.
